title: Delhi Lakshmi Yojana Portal Goes Live, Offers Women Rs 2,500 Monthly Aid
excerpt: The BJP-led Delhi government's flagship welfare scheme launches its online registration portal on August 1, targeting lakhs of eligible women ahead of a Raksha Bandhan rollout.
body:
• Delhi Lakshmi Yojana online registration portal launched on August 1, offering eligible women Rs 2,500 per month in financial assistance
  • Cabinet approved the scheme on July 28 under Chief Minister Rekha Gupta, with Rs 5,100 crore allocated for implementation
  • Eligibility requires Delhi residency of 10+ years, age between 21-60, and family income below Rs 2.5 lakh annually
  • First instalment expected by Raksha Bandhan on August 28, with verification of applicants underway

Portal Opens for Registration

The Delhi government has launched the online registration portal for its Delhi Lakshmi Yojana on August 1, opening the door for eligible women across the national capital to apply for monthly financial assistance of Rs 2,500. The scheme, a key election promise of the BJP government, was formally approved by the Delhi Cabinet on July 28 under the leadership of Chief Minister Rekha Gupta.

https://x.com/gupta_rekha/status/2083485383296463322

Eligible beneficiaries can submit applications through the portal, which will undergo a verification process before approval. The government has said that the first batch of beneficiaries is expected to receive their initial payment by Raksha Bandhan on August 28.

Who Qualifies

The eligibility criteria, finalised by a ministerial committee, set a specific bar for applicants. Women must be between 21 and 60 years of age, must have resided in Delhi for at least 10 years, and must belong to families with a combined annual income below Rs 2.5 lakh. Only one woman per household — the eldest eligible member — can receive the benefit.

Applicants must submit a self-declaration confirming they have no criminal record, and families with members who have criminal records are also excluded. Government employees, income tax payers, pensioners, and women who own four-wheelers are ineligible.

"When a woman in a household becomes financially secure, it accelerates the progress of the family, society and the nation alike."

— Rekha Gupta, Delhi Chief Minister

From Promise to Policy

The scheme, originally conceived as the Mahila Samriddhi Yojana, was renamed Delhi Lakshmi Yojana following a high-level review meeting chaired by the Chief Minister. The rebranding aimed to give the capital's largest financial assistance initiative a distinct local identity.

The Delhi government has earmarked Rs 5,100 crore for the programme, which falls under the Women and Child Development Department. Officials have been directed to ensure the rollout is transparent, simple, and time-bound, with strict verification to prevent fraudulent claims.

The scheme fulfils a flagship pledge from the BJP's Delhi Assembly election campaign. The previous AAP government had promised a similar Rs 1,000-per-month scheme for women — the Mukhyamantri Mahila Samman Yojana — but never implemented it during its second term. The Delhi government later clarified that the AAP-era scheme was never officially notified.

Implementation and Scale

Government estimates suggest the scheme will benefit lakhs of women across the capital. Of the Rs 2,500 monthly payout, reports indicate Rs 1,000 may be disbursed as direct cash, with the remaining Rs 1,500 channelled into a three-year recurring deposit to encourage savings — though the government has not officially confirmed this split.

Required documents include Aadhaar cards, voter identity cards, and supporting family documentation. The application process is fully digital, reflecting Delhi's push toward paperless governance.

What's Next

With the portal now live, the government faces the operational challenge of verifying potentially millions of applications before the August 28 target date. Chief Minister Gupta has tied the initiative to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's broader vision for women-led development, positioning it as a centrepiece of Delhi's welfare architecture for 2026.
nri_angle: NRIs with family in Delhi may need to verify whether female relatives qualify, given the strict residency and income criteria that could exclude middle-class households.
